company_info.company_description: "Smart Energy Answers (SEA) is Australia’s leading provider of solar energy solutions for both residential and commercial clients. With over 7,000 installations nationwide, we offer expert services in solar power, battery storage, EV charging, and pool heating. Our highly skilled team of engineers and technicians delivers custom solutions tailored to each customer’s specific energy needs.As an NETCC Approved Seller, SEA is proud to have received awards such as ProductReview.com’s Best Solar Energy Retailer (2020-2023), Sunwiz Top Solar Company 2022, and EUP Research Top Brand PV Installer 2023.We partner with top-tier brands, including Aiko, SolarEdge, Tesla, and Sungrow, ensuring every installation meets the highest standards. From initial consultation to seamless installation and ongoing support, SEA is committed to empowering Australians to achieve energy independence and reduce energy costs with clean, sustainable solutions.Our CEO, Daniele Lanzetta, is an engineer with over 10 years of industry experience and a trusted expert in the renewable energy industry.Our headquarters are in Sydney, and we serve a wide range of locations, including Melbourne, Canberra, Adelaide, Brisbane, Central Coast, Newcastle, Wollongong, and Orange. For more information, contact us on 1300 732 679 orinfo@smartenergyanswers.com.au.The SEA Advantage:Rely on a trusted, award-winning & Australian-owned national solar installer.Achieve cleaner, innovative, tailored solar solutions with a solid return on investment.Find peace of mind with our performance guarantee & industry-leading warranties."

reviews.review_description: Sales were fast and efficientInstallers were on time if not early and tidyOverall it went very well

We were given the name of Smart Energy Answers by Solar Quotes.We had had problems getting people to quote for solar / battery for our dwelling, because of the heritage listed front face of our terrace in inner city City of Sydney, and also a tricky site. The solar panels had to be installed on both the main house and the granny flat, and the roof pitch of both is steep.But Smart Energy Answers were willing to work with us and we got a great system. It took about fours weeks and two site visits, but we got a quote for a 6.65 kW of solar panels (14 x 475W panels) together with a 24.2 kWh Sigen battery with Gateway SP and inverter for $17,893.70, after Federal and NSW State government rebates. Part of this quote included contingency money, which was good, because we did have problems in installation because of the large run of cables from the front to back of our block. So, the system did come in for the price first quoted.One specification I had was that the system should be Amber compatible, which drove the selection of battery brand.Anyway, it took a bit less than three months from accepting the quote to the completed installation. We were kept informed at every step, and if I had queries, they were answered swiftly.We worked with Conor Gardiner from the outset, and he was really quick to answer my emails after installation.I was also very happy with the installers, who were able to work with the steep roofs and long runs of cables - and the lack of a ceiling cavity! And they quickly noted that our battery would be in the sun for much of the day, and installed an awning.I have learned that the old terrace houses require people who have experience with them, from air conditioning installation to getting a new kitchen. And, it can be more expensive. So while I have heard of people paying less for what we got, they all seem to be installations on recent-build freestanding dwellings, which are cheaper and easier to work with.And, now that four weeks have passed since the installation, we could not be happier. The Sigen App is a joy to behold. We have imported solely 0.7 kWh from the grid since the installation. Our previous rates were 33 cents per kWh, with a $2 per day connection charge.Once Amber install a Smart Meter in the next couple of weeks, we will also be getting paid to export to the grid, and I will see how it goes, but I think we are looking at a pay-back period of less than 4 years.

From quoting through to installation and certification this was the best decision I have made in a long time. Conor did not over-sell but was knowledgeable and efficient. Follow-up communication and the entire process leading up to installation was remarkable. Installation was punctual, the whole system in a day, led by Peter. It worked immediately, entirely as advertised, with fantastic software and sensible information in emails. I could not be happier

Due to the huge demand of home battery installation, it took longer days than I thought to get design proposal completed and installation done. Smart Energy Answer steam still kept high standard of professionalism. Admin team offer me great flexibility on installation schedules. Very happy with their works.I refer my friends to do business with Smart Energy too.

The whole process from initial consultation and quote, to the present where we’ve had the system up and running for about 3 weeks, has been very positive.Everyone from the company has been really professional and genuinely helpful. There were some complications to our installation but they were handled without fuss, and everything has worked out well.We can’t fault the service or the advice we were given, excellent!

Smart Energy Team communicated with me from start to finish. Even well after the installation.They gave me the best price compared to other 5 quotes I’ve received before hand and delivered to what they promised. Never pushed or insisted on what they sell. They listened to what I want and communicated from the start.They are guaranteed a legit business with a massive working warehouse (I’ve been there) not like others that has a shop front and just contracts all the installs. And this is the reason I signed up with SMART ENERGY compared to the other 5. Keep up the good work and awesome customer service.

We are currently in the process of building our new home and were exploring solar energy solutions. Tarek Jawad from SEA provided exceptional support throughout our decision-making journey. He helped us clearly understand our requirements and guided us through the selection process by presenting four tailored options, each with a detailed breakdown of their key benefits.Tarek coordinated seamlessly with us, our builder, electrician, and energy provider to ensure all aspects were considered. His proactive communication and expertise made it easy for us to choose the most suitable solar solution for our needs.
Good price, easy install. Conor was great to deal with.

Accommodating knowledgeable reliable professional - "inherited" rooftop panels when I bought the house = happy with that - so return customer to get battery = very happy with service and equipment performanceGood,yes,yes,yes,yes,yes to above 6 questions

I installed 25 solar panels about two years  ago. Following the Government's offering incentives to install batteries I examined the sense  installing a battery in my situation. I quickly saw the benefit, and reviewed the offerings of a number of suppliers and ultimately determined that the Smart Energies package looked the best for me.I found their sales team and technical  staff to be very professional. Whilst the original install date was delayed by about a month the reason for it  were explained clearly and I were understood and accepted by me. My main contact initially and throughout  the project was Conor Gilbert, his  knowledge of the product offering isI very good and in particular  his patience with an "oldie" like me was great.My property  has some serious slope and step issues to overcome when considering where to install the battery nevertheless, Justin the leader of the install team quickly  confirmed my earlier thinking that the battery could  be  readily installed under the house where there is plenty of head room. The team did a great job installing the battery and integrating it with the rest of then system, The team was very neat and tidy and assured me they would not be leaving until I fully understood the battery operation and associated APP. Justin left me with his phone number indicating that I shouldn't fail to ring him if I had any concerns whatsoever.
Tarek was very knowledgable, helpful and explained every detail and made it easy to understand.

We recently had a 48kW Sig Energy battery and 20kW inverter installed by Smart Energy Answers on the Surf Coast. The installation was first-class, neat, efficient, and professionally executed.From consultation to commissioning, everything was seamless. I dealt directly with Daniel, the owner, who demonstrated deep technical knowledge and a real passion for sustainable energy solutions. It’s clear he values his customers and his installers equally, creating a trustworthy and high-quality service experience.Couldn’t recommend Smart Energy Answers more highly, honest, professional, and genuinely committed to excellence in clean energy.

My experience with Smart Energy Answers has been nothing short of horrible.I accepted a quote and paid a 10% deposit for a 24kw Sigenergy battery on the 28th of May 2025. I was advised that I would have my system installed by end of July.25 June - received email from Smart Energy Answers confirming my installation date 11/07/2511 July - installation did not happen18 July - received bulk email advising delays due to stock shortages. was told I would get an update soon with an installation date.19 August - I emailed SEA requesting an update on my installation as I did not have any update since their last email in July. Nobody responded to my email2 September - I called SEA to get an update. Was advised I would get an installation date ASAP.25 September - I received an email from SEA with a new installation date of 15/10/259 October - I received an email from SEA saying my install date has been moved to the 4/11/25. Note this date is Melbourne cup day. I questioned this but was assured that the installation would go ahead on this date.28 October - I received an email form SEA saying my install had been moved again to 17/11/2529 October - called SEA to complain about the delays and that it is unacceptable to have been waiting for over 5 months with no confirmed installation date. I was asked to email their general email address with my complaint and management would come back to me. Complaint email sent on this day.3 November - Received a call from SEA saying the installation would need to be pushed to December.  I asked for my order to be cancelled and a full refund of my deposit.If this is how they treat customers pre sale, I have no faith that they would provide proper support post sale.

We recently had our solar system installed by Smart Energy Answers, and we couldn’t be happier with the entire experience. From the first consultation by Taimoor Ahmed to the final inspection, the team was professional, knowledgeable, and transparent. Taimoor took the time to explain every step of the process, helped me choose the right system for our energy needs, and handled all the paperwork smoothly.The installation crew was punctual, courteous, and extremely efficient - the panels look great, and the worksite was spotless when they finished. Our system is already performing beyond expectations, and we’ve noticed a significant drop in our power bills!If you’re considering going solar, I can’t recommend Smart Energy Answer highly enough. Excellent service, great communication, and outstanding results!

A huge thank you to Tarek who made this experience seamless. His superior customer service and extensive knowledge of the product really made it easy when making the decision to go with SEA Commercial.He had answers to all my questions and gave me a sense of comfort knowing I was getting value for money. Highly recommend thank you Tarek

I had 8 panels on my home when I purchased 1 year ago  & just wanted a battery  (panels Solar edge installed in Dec2020)I sort 3 quotes through solar quotes but 2 of those given to me did no respond!However I had prompt & frequent exchanges with Connor & was happy to make my choiceThe installation guys were fabulous, really on time, now mess at all & I am very happy, checking my app dailyI have a timber house & a narrow walkway but my battery fits well & I even ahve alittle roof over it!

I have dealt with the Taimoor Ahmed at Smart Energy Answers for a couple of my properties. It has been a great experience every time from quotation to install and ongoing support to ensure both my solar and battery systems are upto the standards. I believe i will always check in with them for all my future solar and battery needs.Great work Taimoor and the support team. Keep up the good work.Munam

I accepted a quotation from Smart Energy Answers  (SEA) on 18 August 2025. The final price was to  be adjusted based on a site inspection which was to  be carried afterwards with the option of cancellation if the adjusted price was too high. As I was travelling overseas it was agreed that the inspection would take place before 18 September 2025.  Despite numerous phone calls and  undertakings by SEA to  do the inspection it did not take place. On 17 September 2025, it was agreed that they would set a time while I was away for an inspection on 13 October 2025, Despite two communications that I sent to SEA while I was away, no inspection was arranged for, or took place on 13 October 2025.After some discussion,  SEA proposed that I  should send them additional  photographs and they would commit to a  firm price on the basis of the photographs without the need for a site inspection.  I provided this, including scaled drawings and  SEA responded but declined to confirm in writing that the price would be fixed. In the end, I sent an  email  to two of their leads, Mark Carroll  and Vikram Siddiqui.  I also asked verbally for the CEO, Daniel Lanzetta to be advised  of the situation.  In the end Vikram phoned and agreement was  reached on a price and design. An installation date of 29  October was set and I was invoiced accordingly. It should be noted that the validity of my rebate expires on 1 November 2025On 28 October, as I had received no message from SEA, I phoned them and then was  told that the installation would not occur on 29 October, but on 31 October ie the day before the rebate expires.  As 31 October is a  day that I have committed to some urgent and  important matters,  and as based on SEA's previous performance it was unlikely that the installation would take place on that day I did not accept this.  Accordingly,  I asked SEA to confirm that they would carryout the installation on the agreed date of 29 October or return  my deposit. I have not had a firm response from  SEA yet. On several previous occasions, because of the non-performance of SEA, I have raised the question of the  return of my deposit as I have had offers from other companies.Be warned: When SEA does  not want to talk  to you, you will find that your call is not taken and goes to a Message Bank (often full). Also, when you do get a chance to talk  to someone, they will often tell you that they will investigate the matter and phone back. Invariably, they do not phone back.Of course, no installation has taken place to date
Very happy with the whole process. Good price, communication and after sale service

The whole process was seamless from getting a quote to installation. Communication was very good and the 10kw system was installed as scheduled and without any issues.I haven't received a power bill yet but the APP is indicating that the system is performing as predicted so I am curious to see the next bill.

I chose Smart Energy Answers to install a 20kw ESY battery due to their moderate business age, competitive price and at the time good ratings.Sadly once the deposit was paid, contact ceased and timeframes weren’t what was promised (make sure to get this in writing as I did). Timeframes advised were 2-3 weeks for inspection and max 8 weeks install. After chasing several people from different departments, I finally had an inspection about 5 weeks out.After inspection, again nothing heard from SEA. Week 7 from deposit I followed up again - advising they advised max 8 week lead time. Again promised follow ups but wasn’t until I chased again that they were looking at installing towards the end of October (12 week lead time). Had SEA escalate this as it was a breach of their sale/contract. They came back after a few days finally scheduling in on the 9th week.Installation team arrived within the time frame shared. They got to work and limited times without power which was beneficial whilst working from home. Assisted with some aspects including cutting another access panel in garage ceiling for cable pathway. No attempt at cleaning was made, but that only took a quick sweep and vacuum so wasn’t fussed on that.The day after install, found the smart meter was reporting very odd values - often 1/3 of what should be - flagged this to SEA team. This has also resulted in 2-3 kw per day from grid being used even though load was below threshold of inverter (average appears to be 0.5kw per day) and a large load showing that’s not there when compared to Energy Australia and Sungrow.Case was logged 2 weeks ago, have followed up and have been advised “ Our schedule is fully booked at the moment, but we are doing our best to secure a date…”.Still waiting on SEA to resolve the issue. I do not recommend purchasing from SEA as it is clear they are over booked and do not have time to resolve issues with their installations.
Excellent customer service and excellent installer,installation is fantastic and working well
The installation process was seamless. The installation lead was friendly and super helpful.The set up was simple and easy to use. All in all - very happy with the installation.
Installation was tidy, on time and a very polite installer went above and beyond with the installation and explained everything very well. Can thoroughly recommend them!

I had a fantastic experience with Smart Energy Answers, from start to finish. The whole process — booking, site inspection, installation, and aftercare — was smooth and professional. Communication was clear at every step, and the team always kept me informed, which gave me a lot of confidence throughout the journey.The installation itself was completed on time with great attention to detail, and the quality of work was excellent. When I later faced an issue with my battery, SEA’s responsiveness really stood out. They immediately raised a ticket with the manufacturer and made sure I was kept fully updated with phone calls along the way. As soon as the manufacturer provided the replacement, SEA acted quickly to resolve the issue and had everything back on track without delay.Overall, I’m very happy with Smart Energy Answers. Their communication, professionalism, and customer-first approach made the whole experience easy and stress-free. I would highly recommend them to anyone considering solar and battery solutions.
Good communication and clear process. Happy with the installation and customer service.

The sales process was very smooth with a great explanation of all the options and their quote was several thousand less than the second quote I received.However, after I paid the deposit the communication was all down hill. You move from talking to their slick and knowledgeable sales team to their lack luster operations team. I had to email SEA several times to organise an installation date and when I finally got one it was moved around several times in the week before.Our installation was complex - adding full home back up via the Sigenergy Gateway in our townhouse garage involved a double looping of wires ~10m to the main complex switchboard and wiring in our existing solar panels while decommissioning the existing inverter. This took a team of 4 a whole day to complete which is clearly more than they had budgeted for.In the process of installation they managed to cut our NBN HFC wire which then required an NBN call out to fix leaving us without internet for 4 days. Accidents happen.The main issue with the installation is that they never installed the required fire alarm when installing in a garage - even after following up with them several times post installation. Given this is a safety requirement I believe this is inexcusable.

Had my battery installed.Not working correctly and feeding electricity into the grid rather than using it in the house.My electricity usage has actually gone up.They refuse to resolve despite repeated contact and have now stopped responding at all, presumably just hoping I will go away.

This company did a terrific job installing my new batteries. The sales process was straightforward and a good price. The installation was done by a team of 4 guys, all of them very polite and they did a really tidy job. They turned up on time and it took as long as they said it would. They also replaced a broken tile. They helped me set up the app and made sure it was all connected to the grid and working properly before they left. Couldn’t be happier with this company. They even contacted me to check I was happy afterwards.

There was no hard sales approach where you know within 5 mins into the conversation the person is only out to make a dollar!Right from the start Smart Energy Answers reps were interested in listening, offer solutions and advice to custom a battery install to my needs. installation process was efficient, professional, put up with “ this guys” constant questions patiently and completed everything to a high quality finish.Definitely will continue an association with SMA for future upgrades and works.NOT to be confused with Smart Energy who I cannot rate at all.

Smart Energy Answers, from the initial quote to the install have been a pleasure to deal with.From providing the quote within a short period of time to advising of all the stages as they occurred and providingthe documentation required for Strata the process was relatively simple. The install occurred in a single day with the team working extremely hard making for a very long day for them, with everything being finished just after the sun went down. They asked about my preferences for conduit placing, battery placement so that things would look very neat and tidy. Hilariously the day after the install it started raingin for the next 2 weeks so it took a while before I could find out how good the solar panels were. Once the sun finally came out, magic, the panels seem to be extremely efficient even though it is late winter. There was a slight issue with the PW3 battery shutting down on the first really sunny day, but after the issue being reported they took care of everything, informing Tesla who had a reasonably fast turnaround time with new FW being loaded onto the system and no issues since. I'd recommend them to anyone who wants solar panels and battery. Very impressed.
I found them very responsive to my questions and they gave good advice

I found the sales team engaging and professional, willing and able to answer all my queries. The pre-install inspection was very helpful to identify the best location.  The installation team contacted me the day before and arranged to deliver the battery prior to installation. On the day they turned up on time and installed the battery efficiently and quickly in the rain.
Very nice and professional team, from quoting to communicating to am the installation process; punctual, clean and tidy
Team arrived on time and ready for the job. Battery installed efficiently in my desired location. All up and running in a couple of hours. The guys left the site clean and tidy.

A disappointing experience with my battery purchase. Changed the quote price mid installation. Failed to get the battery to work on the day. The only time I heard from them over the new few weeks was their accounts department chasing payment (for a battery that didn't work). Took them a month to come back and get the battery working.

I recently had solar installed with Smart Energy Answers and the whole experience was outstanding. The sales and quoting process was clear, professional, and easy to follow. They gave me straightforward advice without any pressure and helped tailor the system to my needs.The installation team from Smart Energy Answers were excellent – punctual, polite, and efficient. They kept everything tidy during the job and left the site spotless when they were done.Their customer service has been just as impressive. They took care of the grid connection after the install, which made things really simple, and also walked me through how to monitor the system and use the charger so I felt completely confident.Overall, I couldn’t recommend Smart Energy Answers highly enough. A professional and reliable company that makes the entire solar process stress-free from start to finish.
From the start to the finish this company has been really easy to work with super happy to answer all questions and the installer was amazing.

SEA’s quote and sales team were excellent, providing full details of the process and no surprise costs at the other end of the process.The installers were polite, efficient and cleaned up well.  They were over an hour late arriving which was a bit of a pain for me as I had to go to night shift.  Other than that they were excellent. They explained the connection and ensured the app was installed properly on my phone.  Very happy and would gladly recommend to anyone.

I was fortunate to receive a quotation for SEA. Their proposal and professional swayed me in selecting them for the installation of a Powerwall 3. Their price was not the cheapest, however it transpired that I was right in selecting SEA. They met every deadline that they had committed to, despite this being an incredibly tough month (July 2025). Their installers did a very good job and provided additional advice on the day of installation, regarding the positioning of the battery.I now have room for an additional Powerwall Expansion if this is needed at a later stage.I have no hesitation in recommending SEA

After reviewing the information on the web site on a Wednesday, I arranged to get 2 companies to quote. One responded immediately and the other the next day. By the end of Friday the sales staff had visited, and I received my quotes over the weekend. That is a very fast quoting process!We made our choice and the system was professionally installed in half a day about a month later. The whole process was painless and has been working well for about a month so far.
Very happy with our 24kw Sigenergy battery from Smart Energy Answers. They provided excellent customer service and communication. Highly recommended

Smart Energy Answers connect a 25kwh battery to our existing solar panels. The whole process was excellent from the initial consultation to the final installation by a partner company. The options were clearly presented and the final option we selected was competitively priced. Initially, there was an issue with the distribution of solar power to the grid in preference to the battery, but this was quickly resolved by a remotely installed software upgrade.Smart Energy Answers are a professional company using quality products and I am happy to recommend it to anyone looking to instal a solar battery.
Good communication and follow up from start to end, and after ‘end’…
Everything was easy and hassle free and we were kept up to date and informed every step of the way

Sales process was good and they shared lots of information, but it went downhill quickly from when I paid a deposit.Site visit was rescheduled on the day, then when they did come they tried to add 2 more items to my bill for things I'd already checked with the sales person were included. I had to negotiate down again.Installation was rescheduled the day before, then not completed within a day (due to weather, fair enough). But they never followed up to schedule the second half and I had to chase yet again.About a week after install my power goes out, so call support and they file an "urgent" ticket. I call again 3 hours later and nobody has even looked at the ticket Another hour later and a few phone calls later they finally get the installer to call me and we can sort it out. Frustratingly if the shutdown and restart procedure instructions they'd given me were correct I would have been able to solve it myself. I'm still chasing support to give me correct instructions weeks later.No guidance was given on when I'd be connected to the grid for exports so I'm just waiting...

Sales process was straightforward with questions answered promptly and changes I requested for the system capacity were amended promptly and without fuss. This included an amendment to the green loan which was handled well without issue.Installation required a full replacement of the main switchboard. The installer took the opportunity to tidy up a very old board with a modern switchboard and did this at very reasonable cost despite it taking longer than anticipated.Connection to Amber has been very straightforward and I’m seeing the results already.Customer service post install has been very good with follow up calls from them to check everything is working as expected.

SEA were interested in my specific design requirements, and provided good advice on system design.  The price was very competitive.Installation went well, although there was some miscommunication on a variation to the price (due to a long cable run between the battery and switchboard) which led to last minute haggling on price (while the installation was underway).The final presentation of the panels which faced the road was excellent.Initially the battery app which provides info on demand/supply was very flaky which led to some long periods where the app was not working (longest period was 6 weeks).  Responses from SME to solve the problem was often very slow (initial email/phone call responses were very prompt, but it often took a week to a fortnight to get technical support).  A new version of the app has worked well for the last 6 weeks, and there have been no drop outs.

We had a 20kw solar system and 24kwh battery installed through Smart Energy Answers (SEA) by one of their partner companies in Canberra, Summit and Shore Energy.We are really happy with the system, the installation process was smooth on the day, installers were polite, left everything tidy, and explained everything to us. The system is working as intended.The customer service was good too; admin staff at SEA are friendly and punctual with responses.Noting that we understand it is a busy time with the battery rebate and there were some rain delays, there were some things that weren't as smooth as expected, including mixed messaging we received around installation date (different messaging from SEA directly and installer multiple times), our site inspection prior to installation was undertaken by one of SEA's other company partners who didn't end up installing for us, and we requested ethernet connection to the battery/inverter instead of wifi which hasn't been connected yet (although SEA were quick to raise a job to complete this afterwards when we notified them).It was appreciated that they could do the install on a Sunday for us to make sure the job was done on time.Overall we are very happy with the outcome and would recommend Smart Energy Answers and their partner companies.

They wouldn’t come to site to check if the inverter was wired in 240VAC cabling to the fuse box. They gave me what they called a quote and I called an estimate which included a new 240VAC cable from the inverter even as I told them they didn’t need to . Ultimately they did send someone to site to check and the 240VAC cable was as I told them and they dropped the price by $500.
Installation was tidy, punctual, and complete.Efficiently done with very pleasant and friendly personnel both on site and in the office.
We have been really impressed by the after sales service and the product (panels and battery) provided for us by Smart Energy Answers and Sungrow… thankyou

The sales and quoting process was superior to all others as it was based on a site inspection. The installation process was excellent. Some unforeseen problems were encountered along the way as to where to site the battery but the installer went above and beyond expectations to find a very satisfactory solution. Also, very mindful of our need for council approval given we are in a heritage overlay area. Hand off could have been a bit more thorough but this was more than offset by excellent after sales service.All in all, a very good job.

16kWh Sigenergy solutionExisting 9.6kW PV system with Fronius Symo 8.2-3-MI found the team to be knowledgeable, responsive, offered competitive pricing, and delivered an excellent solution for my use case (3-phase home with existing PV solution). Communications could sometimes have been a little better (e.g. communicating the final design, the process for the NSW government PDRS battery incentive) but everything came together in the end. Very happy with the solution (currently 2 months since installation).

The sales process was very consultative with clear communication on viable options. The link between sales consultant, designers and installation was very smooth.Any questions were responded to quickly and when it looked like we couldn’t have our first option they didn’t give up but kept working with us to understand the site to get the optimal outcome.

I had a fantastic experience with Smart Energy Answers! From the initial consultation to the final installation, the entire process was smooth, professional, and transparent. The team took the time to answer all my questions and helped me choose the best solar solution for my home. Installation was quick and tidy, and the crew was respectful and knowledgeable (shoutout to installer Timothy Duggan). I've already started seeing the benefits on my energy bill, and I feel great knowing I’m using clean energy. Highly recommend this company to anyone considering going solar!

Very good quality company with a site inspection to ensure all factors taken into account.  Flexible approach to negotiation on price and the guys installing were very professional.  My roof access was challenging and the weather was bad but there was no complaints and they got on with the job.

Smart energy answers have a very good process, lots of communication and follow up. In particular I’d like to praise the installers, my roof in inner west Sydney was not easy access and without complaint the installers went about their business without complaint and completed a professional job. Thank you.

At the end of last year I finally decided to bite the bullet and install solar panels and a battery. We just changed electricity suppliers and they recommended Smart Energy Answers. The quotation process was easy and done online and we were happy with the result. In the process we were offered a discount on the battery but it turned out by the time we accepted the quote the battery was out of stock and we would have to wait for more stock to arrive. We were offered the same discount on a what looks to be possibly a better battery adding extra capacity for a slightly higher cost which we were actually very happy about.The installer was really great. He made sure that everything was working properly (there were a couple of hiccups) before he left. Turned up when expected and tidied up afterwards.  He also walked us through the app and made sure we could log in and that everything was running as expected.  Really very helpful.Everything is working well and we are very happy.Still don't fully get all the stuff about all the certificates but that looks to have sorted itself out.

We had a 10kw solar system installed about a year ago.Overall the process was great.The sales quote process was good, we always spoke to the same person and they were knowledgeable and happy to send us different quotes for different inverters/panels.Installation was great, no issues, clean and efficient.They organised the connection to the grid, so we just had to organise the app on our phones and once it was connected it worked.Overall I would recommend them.

We have an existing 8.3kW solar system, installed about 2 years ago. I have been looking at batteries for a few months but prices were too high. The latest NSW Government rebates, combined with the introduction of numerous new brands this year, have substantially reduced prices. My initial call to SEA was with Sam, who was very knowledgeable and answered all my questions, while also providing valuable advice. My initial enquiry was for a 10kW battery but Sam explained that with the ESY Smarthome battery, I could purchase more 5kW modules with even higher discounts. I was able to increase my battery system from 10 to 25 kW (150% increase) for just an extra price increase of 25%. It was a no-brainer to spend the extra and we are so glad we did. It has virtually cut out our energy bill now, having also replaced our gas hot water with a heat pump.The installation was also excellent and was a very neat job. SEA asked me to send photos and measurements of our location, which made the installation very smooth. We then changed our provider to Amber and use their partner Evergen which provides the automatic power management system. I embarked on the solar journey via SolarQuotes (SQ) despite having a small North Roof which gets shaded at midday in winter, a larger unshaded South Roof and a small Flat Roof which is shaded in the morningI ended up choosing the Enphase system not because of the supposed shading benefits but because my electricity box is exposed in a street lane & any inverter installed near there would be subject to vandalism or installed with another ugly guard box. I had read that the Enphase system didnt require a main inverter to be installed but only required a small device called "Envoy" which could potentially fit in the existing electricity box or better still, installed inside the house next to any existing sub-boardOut of the firms SQ referred me to, I decided to pay a premium for Smart Energy Answers (SEA) as I preferred a larger firm than ‘one man band’ companies as I thought that they would provide better after sales support in case any issues arose. SEA also claimed to provide a “quality control follow-up within 4wks from installation” & a “performance guarantee” which is supposed to provide compensation if the output of the installed system is less than estimates generated by their sales program. The estimate considers the length of day & avg weather conditions each month (ie how many rainy, cloudy, & sunny days), azumith + pitch of the panels, and any shading from nearby objectsAt first, SEA’s sales consultant insisted that the Enphase system had to be installed with an iBoard, a box which looks as big as any inverter however after a bit of prodding he said that if I paid SEA a non-refundable $200 (if I didnt proceed with SEA) or a 10% deposit, they’d send someone to make a site inspection.  This was arranged for 25/3Sadly the site inspector (SI) had no idea as well! I found this confusing as SEA claims to be a ‘Enphase Gold Installer.’ The only thing the SI was useful for was to get himself on the roof & take more accurate measurements of the North roof which resulted in another 2 panels fitting onto the plan. However, he failed to measure the South roof properly (the installer still had to change his layout) & no consideration was given to tilting any of the panels on the Flat Roof (so they could self clean) or the last row of the South RoofA couple of days later SEA advised that the installation team would be available on 3/4 between 0700-0830. At 1000, the 1st member of the installation team arrived. I was surprised he was wearing a t-shirt from another company as I'm pretty sure the SEA sales consultant said they had their own in-house installers although this didnt concern me at the time. This installer also didnt know whether the Envoy could sit inside the meter box or the sub-board inside the house but after a call to his boss, he proceeded to start installing the Envoy inside the meter box. The boss arrived ½hr later & he took some quick measurements on all 3 roofs which resulted in a more optimal positioning for the 8 panels on the South roof. Another member of the installation team arrived after that & together, the 3 man team proceeded to install the system. I would have preferred to have the conduit of cables from the roof to the electricity box go inside the wall cavity instead of having the conduit on the outside of the house ( as per https://www.solarquotes.com.au/blog/solar-installation-video-mb2069/ which was also suggested by 1 of the other SQ quoters) however this was not to be. After the panels were installed, the boss set up the Envoy to communicate with my Wifi although as the sun was starting to set, we couldnt see whether everything was running smoothly. As the Envoy was installed inside the electricity box, the iBoard was not required although SEA has not refunded me for this (it retails for >$750)The next day 4/4 the SEA support team got to work with the paperwork to my energy retailer to arrange a new smart meter to be installed. Everything was going very well within the support team.  There were many team members, each with different tasks. This is exactly what I expected and was very pleased with their efficiency. The team forwarded me a user manual & then set me up with the Enphase app (EApp) however it was then I started to notice a few issues:-The “Energy” tab of the EApp was recording all the ‘production’ [blue] plus my imports [grey] as being ‘consumed’ [orange]. I assumed at the time that this was because I was not connected to the grid yet-I also asked whether I was self-consuming the electricity I was generating and the reply came back from SEA as yes (this answer proved incorrect)-there was nothing displayed in the “Array” tab of the EApp so I could not see how the individual panels were performingOn 11/4 the panels were populated in the “Array” tab. I dont know whether this delay was caused by the installer not passing on the information to SEA or a delay at SEA’s end. Anyhow, the data showed that one of the panels hadnt produced any electricity since the day of install. A tick for the Enphase system as this may not have been noticed in a normal string system! I waited a few more days as I thought that SEA would be monitoring the system in the background & would inform me as such and/or fix things in the background however this didnt happen. On 14/4 I emailed the team advising my concern. One of the original installers quickly came back on 17/4 & determined that one of the solar panels was not working however as he did not have any spares he would have to come back at a later dateBy 28/4 my system was connected to the grid & my house was using the electricity generated & exporting the excess however the EApp was still showing all the ‘production’ [blue] plus my imports [grey] as being ‘consumed’ [orange]. After weekly follow up emails to SEA’s support team, the boss installer came back on 23/5 to replace the panel & to rewire the Envoy. The EApp was now finally showing both imports & exports!I wish I could end the review here and be satisfied for the most part however:After the dead panel was replaced there was a string of sunny days in late May so I was able to start comparing what the actual output of the system was with what SEA had forecast in their quote. 12.6, 11.9, 11.8, 11.7kWh was achieved on these perfectly sunny, cloudless days in late May. However, SEA’s quote said the system should be generating an avg of 12.8kWh in June after considering cloudy & rainy days! Days would only be getting shorter up until the June equinox & the output I was getting on sunny days in late May would only be getting lower on sunny days in June. Basic maths told me that even if it was sunny every single day in June, I would have no hope of getting to the predicted avg of 12.8kWh! I emailed my concerns on 29/5 as well as asking whether the “quality control follow-up within 4 weeks from installation” would be undertaken as it was now nearly 7 wks since the original installationMeanwhile, I was still experiencing discrepancies with the EApp: Ausgrid’s data was saying I was importing ~40% & exporting 15% more electricity than the import/export numbers on the EApp. Enphase help files suggest that numbers should be within a 2.5% tolerance level. I emailed the support team on 5/6 with my findings, including pictures showing the differences from both the EApp & my energy retailer. I followed up on 18/6, 25/6, and 27/6. This was increasingly concerning for me as I did not expect SEA, an Enphase Gold Installer, to not know or not reply to this issueOn 28/6 I received a call from SEA who:-claimed solar radiation was lower this yr than previous yrs & that was the cause of my lower generation (this is false as Ive checked with friends whove been getting same generation on sunny days in the middle of June as previous yrs)-claimed the “quality control follow-up within 4 wks from installation” was nothing more than the ability for me to talk to SEA about issues and not SEA being proactive to see if anything else was wrong with systemOn 29/7 boss installer came back & advised nothing was wrong with the wiring. Despite having only a fridge & modem on, Enphase still recorded a correlation between production & consumption. This provided further proof that something was still wrong as the discrepancy between Enphase and my energy retailer persists. SEA has yet to respond to my latest email (3 wks and counting)And so here we are. This is the longest review Ive done & Ive had to cut it

Bottom Line Up Front: System is working and installation faults were fixed but only after the Operations Director got personally involved.The pre-sales process was very comprehensive and provided good information.  Unfortunately, on the installation day the installers decided to modify the design and placed 3 panels on an eastern roof face rather than a northern roof face without discussing this change.  Unfortunately, as I was suffering from a back injury at the time, I was not actively supervising the installation and so this was not picked up until the installation was completed and the installer had left.  I notified the company t the time and requested a revised performance assessment to allow for comparative assessment of this change. I noticed that the overall production was down by about 10% and this was particularly the case in winter.  At this time I also noticed that the system did not seem to be producing the expected output.  In monitoring the system, I noticed that it was only operating on half the panels as the northern and eastern arrays had not been connected. This was not picked up by the electrician when he was testing the system and relied on myself diagnosing the problem for the technical support staff.Initial communication in relation to these issues with the sales and support area was not great and the company seems to prefer phones calls over emails, which makes keeping records more challenging.  Things really only got better once the case was escalated and the operations director, Sam, got involved personally as clearly this was not up to his expectations in terms of the installation or post install support.  Sam acknowledged the issues and noted that the installers are not supposed to make changes without both customer and engineering approval.  Sam phoned me at agreed times, assured me that he was more than willing to move the panels and provided a comparative performance study examining the difference in time of performance for self-consumption.  The array connection issue was solved after three days, and the panels have been moved to a northern face to optimise performance.It has not been a smooth experience and undoubtably the company will have a look at things to try to improve.  I would suggest that people double check with the installer that they have the agreed design and periodically have a look to confirm that that is what is being done and at the end if the installation confirm with the electrician that all panels are identified as being present by the inverter. It would also seem to be a simple QA check for the company to use remote monitoring after the installation to confirm that all the panels are reporting as present.I am rating the installation as 1 star largely because of the issues on the day and the lack of communications from the installers in relation to the unapproved changes and the 3 return visits that were required. Customer service was really only driven by Sam getting involved, prior to that I would have rated it as poor.  Value and Quality are 3* largely because the system is too new to make proper assessments, it is now producing as per the design and performance estimates.

reviews.review_description: Good advice. Lots of contact. Quick install. Very happy with our installation.
Sales process was great and sales person was very knowledgeable. Installer was great and ran me through the entire setup as well as the testing the system extensively.

The sales quoting process was great. The sales person spent a lot of time modifying my system as I compared systems from other installers and increased my understanding of my options.I had to hold off on going ahead with it as we were waiting to move back into our home that we had been renting out and initially our builder (renovations) wanted us to hold off until after work had been completed. Eventually we decided to go ahead and organised our finances with the bank. By the time we had decided to accept it there had been some cost increases. I believe the sales consultant when he actively worked to reduce the impact to the cost on us.The only part that upset me was regarding an application to increase the inverted capacity above 10kW with Ausgrid being the grid operator. The system was using microinverters and originally had an inverter capacity of 11.5kW. The sales consultant said that we could apply to exceed the 10kW at a cost of $750. I asked about why it cost so much, and I was told by the sales consultant that it was because the operator had to send someone out to do a manual site inspection where a local transformer was checked to see if it could handle additional capacity. I was told that they would tell us exactly what we would be able to have inverted so that we may even be able to expand later on.Eventually the design engineer came back and told us that the grid operator did not approve the additional capacity. I asked for correspondence between SEA and the grid operator, and it was clear that no real assessment was done. Ausgrid simply said that SEA needed to show how the system would be 10kW or less of inverter capacity, that 11.5 was greater than 10. I queried it with the design engineer, cc'ing the sales consultant and he said it was a technical assessment not a physical one, that the operator checks their transmission systems according to their network. But this is simply not true, Ausgrid wrote to SEA:"Single phase connections must have a maximum inverter capacity of 10kVA. Your application indicates 11.52kVA. Can you review and advise how the inverter capacity will be reduced to <10KVA. Note – export limiting while required for the battery and solar combination does not negate the maximum 10kVA PV IES requirement".So essentially, $750 was paid for the operator to check if 11.5 was larger than 10. It also delayed installation time by over a month whilst we waited on the results of the assessment. The sales consultant was cc'd in all these emails and never replied. The design engineer stopped replying to the issue.In the end I went forward with it as I was happy with the system and other reviews I had read on Solar Quotes. The sales consultant had originally put in a lot of time on the quote and sales process, just left me down after acceptance during this issue.Once the system size was reduced, the installation was scheduled very quickly, I think the next week. 4 men came out to install the solar panels, tesla battery and associated equipment. At the end of the day the solar was installed but they could not get the battery online. Another technician from SEA came 2 days later (offered to come the next morning but I was unavailable) and got the battery online. They were polite, professional, punctual, and everything was cleaned up on completion.It took a few weeks to get the system registered on the national database so I could sign up for a feed in agreement with my energy provided, but not sure where the delay came from here, not necessarily on SEA end. Customer service was pretty good whilst going back and forth regarding completion of installation paperwork and database registration.So far, the system has been and running for about a month. I can monitor the panels themselves with the enphase app and the battery in the tesla app. Everything appears to be running very well.From a technical needs aspect, I am very happy with the enphase with micro inverters and the whole house backup of the single phase with the tesla battery.Overall, I am very happy with the system. I feel like I got a good/reasonable price and was not ripped off. The quoting process/sales consultation and installation was good. Just a little disappointed with what seems to be a misunderstanding of the limitations of a single-phase installation and any means of applying to exceed these on the behalf of the sales consultant, the design engineer or both; as well as how it was handled. Even now, I am not sure if I have any ability in the future to expand my system except maybe with an additional battery. Hopefully as the grid is re-worked for more solar, these limitations are changed.I would recommend SEA, I would certainly speak to them again if I do want another battery and for my parents when they look to get a battery, increase the solar. I would also recommend using solar quotes to initiate the whole process and as a source of information when researching.

I had specifically asked for an on-site meeting - they were the only ones to bother to attend. The others called and sent me a quote.The others were cheaper - but were suggesting cheap brands. A busbar was loose...Overall, I would not recommend Smart Energy Answers. It seems departments hardly communicate which leads to miss managed consumer experiences. I just hope that our system has no issues for a long time because I do not want to have to deal with them again.

So I went ahead and purchased panel and a battery form smart energy answers.Sales pitch was great, promises were amazing!Australian company, in the industry for many years, if every had any future problems- it would be resolved…. Bla bla blaGot my system installed mid August, paid 8.5k….At the time of installation, the Alpha ESS battery was showing a fault.Was told it could be managed remotely- stupid me for believing and paid for the whole system upfront.Long story short, it’s now early Oct, and I still have a faulty battery.I’ve had two other people visit, one inspector and another person to solve the problem-I have been in touch with smart every answers since installation.They have been really nice about it however they tell me that Alpha (the battery people) are rubbish at returning calls, and so are other people they are waiting on.I wish I didn’t pay the fees as I could have used the money elsewhere- and only paid once everything was up and running.Also, I was told that everything would be done on my behalf in terms of contacting my energy provider and switching over….This wasn’t done initially and I had to make those calls back and forward between my energy provider and smart energy to follow up the paperwork needed.All in all, this process thus far has not been as smooth as I imagined.

We requested three quotes through SolarQuotes and Smart Energy Answers were the first to get back to us. They were professional and seemed to know what they were talking about. Their proposal included HT-SAAE HT54-18X 415W panels which I was cautious about as they weren't on the SolarQuotes "Trusted Brands" chart. I questioned it a number of times and was notably concerned but the Smart Energy Answers salesman convinced me they were great panels and I wouldn't be disappointed. I asked if they could provide another brand of panel that was on the SolarQuotes Trusted Brands chart to which they said no.We received two other quotes: One was considerably more expensive, and while the other was cheaper - they didn't fill us with confidence, so we went with SEA.The proposal included the option of Enphase IQ7A Microinverters or a SolarEdge HD Wave Genesis Inverter. We agreed to the proposal of 19x HT54-18X 415W panels (19x 415W = 7.8kW) and 19x Enphase IQ7A Microinverters (19x 349W = 6.6kW). They wanted payment in full prior to the installation which we found a bit odd but after raising our concerns, they allowed us to pay a portion of the bill in the morning of installation and the remainder after the installation.Installation was reasonably smooth, the A grade electrician running the installation was great. He was happy to answer all my annoying questions and accomodate our request to locate the solar switchboard to a more discrete location, rather than next to our front door. He also sent one of his guys to terminate an ethernet cable to the Enphase Envoy unit a few weeks later for no charge.The panels were installed on a flat roof, all facing north and required Tilt Frames. While the proposal stated "All Black anodised racking", the tilt frames are all silver which we can see from our backyard. A few of the tilts are also not straight which bothers me every time I see them!As for performance - I've been monitoring the solar system closely over the last 4 months by capturing the data directly from the Envoy and graphing the metrics in Grafana. I noticed relatively early on that the microinverters did not get close to their 349W maximum output. I put it down to being winter in Melbourne but as sunnier spring days hit, the maximum output of the entire system was still peaking at around 5.6kW, and not the 6.6kW we were expecting. It wasn't until I raised the question on a forum that someone pointed out that while the panels can produce 415w, it's at 13A and the IQ7A microinverters have a maximum continuous input of 10.2A . This effectively drops our 415W panels down to 300W which leaves us with a total maximum output of approx. 5.6kW. To quote another installer who looked at the panel datasheet provided by Smart Energy Answers: "Your panels have a max power current, Imp = 13.14A but the IQ7A clips at 10A so straight away at a Vmp of 31.6, you're down to 316 theoretical watts. You'll never see the panels producing 31.6V, that wish is granted at 25ºC. On a sunny day Vmp is down to 28.56V. 28.56 x 10 = 285.6W." This is the kind of expertise I was expecting from Smart Energy Answers.We paid just over $10,000 for a 7.8kW system that we expected to output 6.6kW, to only be left with 5.6kW. Needless to say, we're quite disappointed. I've reached out to Smart Energy Answers about our findings but have yet to hear back.

After very friendly communication and suitable advice about our solar system requirements the sales person at SEA provided us with 3 suitable proposals. He gave us a final decision date, about 1 week, on these 3 quotes.When we failed to make a decision within that time frame and came back to him a couple days later with our selected choice he told us the price of that system had gone up, rather steeply, from $5603 to $6819 after rebate. All these supposed to be done by them and their licensed electrician!!!!So the technical part of issue and my contact summary are below:- my area is experiencing high voltage upto 250v (standard 240v), the grid provider has now fixed it.- if the inverter was installed according to Australian Standard, it should tolerate voltage range upto 255v which should not be an issue- The inverter was installed as default setting (the electrician did not select AUS option in configuration), which cause the system constantly stopped working when the grid reached 250v.- I contacted the company, they blame the grid provider...- I contacted the grid provider, it will take them a while to fix it (I agree they also have responsibility to keep this in the range)- I contacted SMA, the German inverter manufacturer, and been advised the system was not configured according to AUS standard- I contacted Solar Quotes, been advised high voltage is very common issue, the solar company should test the area before signing the contract and let me know the issue for decision making, which obviously they did not.- I contacted Consumer Affair, been asked to contact the retailer again...- I then went back to the solar company, but been told the electrician is too busy to come back...so they got me access to the system and ask me to fix it myself...good job!After all this mess, the system finally back online however, I missed the first summer after installation...Impressive
